newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jauch & Huebener - 'Unison alternative by end June'.
newsitem.headline: Jauch & Huebener - 'Unison alternative by end June'.

text.p: German insurance broker Jauch & Huebener said on Friday it will decide by June on an alternative its current strategic alliance with US broker Johnson & Higgins.

The company, Germany's largest broker, said it would "evaluate thoroughly all alternatives in the operation of its international business," following the merger of J&H with US broker Marsh & McLennan.

Jauch & Huebener is currently part of the Unison network, of which J&H is a leading member. However Marsh & McLennan owns Germany's second largest broker Gradmann Holler, and a rival to its own operation.

The US merger "could lead to a situation in which the 35- years-old global Unison net has to be replaced by an alternative, taking account of customers' interests," Jauch & Huebener said in a statement.

In a meeting earlier this week, Johnson & Higgins and Jauch & Huebener decided to continue co-operation for the time being. But a final decision on future alternatives would be taken before the end of June, Jauch & Huebener said. At present, it was too early to give concrete solutions the statement said.

Unison is active with 200 offices in 70 countries. Jauch & Huebener, which handles all its international business via the network, is the Unison partner for Germany, Austria, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Russia.
